title: Tailorly Studio
summary: The AI resume tailor, built out of my own job hunt. A base profile keeps every rewrite grounded in your real experience while the AI lifts each bullet to the recruiter bar, then it drafts the cover letter, outreach email and interview prep to match.

images.caption: The workspace: base profile with skill pills, target job panel and the get hire ready checklist.
Onboarding: upload an existing resume and the parser pre-fills every step, or start from blank.
Landing page: the promise, the numbers and the industries it is tuned for.
The full flow: paste a JD and watch the rest get drafted, step by step.

stories.title: Born from my own job hunt
stories.body: I got tired of rewriting the same bullets for every posting. The bet never changed: a base profile keeps the AI grounded in your real experience, so nothing gets invented. Good work, just reframed to the bar.

stories.title: What I would do differently
stories.body: Ship the ATS parser earlier and tighten it hard. The moment the model had clean, structured bullets to work from, every later step got easier.

title: Kiva
summary: The quoting and invoicing app for UK tradespeople. Speak a job out loud and AI writes a professional quote, then handles invoicing and getting paid.
role: Founder and sole full stack engineer

images.caption: Kiva landing page: speak a job, send a quote in seconds.

stories.title: The core loop already works
stories.body: Kiva is still in progress, but the heart of it is real. A tradesperson speaks the job out loud, FastAPI turns that into structured quote data, and React Native renders a professional quote in seconds. Invoicing and follow ups take over from there.

stories.title: Why tradespeople first
stories.body: Quote writing eats evenings. Most trades still quote through WhatsApp or pen and paper, then chase payment one message at a time. Voice first quoting meets them where the work happens, so the paperwork happens once instead of three times.

title: SimpleFin
summary: A market research and portfolio workspace I built as my own venture over two full years: live indices, watchlists, stock deep dives, benchmark comparisons and a personal dashboard, all in one app.
role: Founder and sole full stack engineer

images.caption: Market overview: live indices, charts, the daily brief and market breadth at a glance.
Portfolio workspace: watchlists, holdings, simulation mode and asset allocation.
Stock deep dive: key statistics, financials, dividends, price history and simulation.
Benchmarks: any stock against the S&P 500 with beta, drawdown and correlation.
Sector performance and market movers, updated through the session.
Real traction, straight from Google Analytics.

stories.title: Two years, one pair of hands
stories.body: SimpleFin was my own venture and I built it full time for two years, every layer of it: market data, dashboards, the lot. Watching 157K people show up in the analytics was the moment it stopped being a side thing and became a product.

stories.title: What I would do differently
stories.body: Bring the design system in earlier. Retrofitting consistency across six major screens taught me a lot, but starting with it on day one would have been kinder to both the code and the users.

title: PXO Production Intelligence
summary: Production finance and planning intelligence for a global VFX studio: bid scenario worksheets, planning networks, portfolio dashboards and document pipelines, working across six currencies and four languages.
ownershipText: Built for Pixomondo: production finance workspace, in-role

images.caption: Bid planning: a network of weekly bids, versions and the active path, over an editable timeline.
Bid worksheet: 180 shots at once with facility, per-discipline day rates and multi-currency totals.
Portfolio dashboard: revenue by studio, cost breakdown and margin by project across regions.
Settings: four languages and six currencies, with live number formatting.
Document management: EFC workbooks wired to bid files for reconciliation.

stories.title: The workflow before this
stories.body: Bids, forecasts and status reports used to live in separate workbooks. PXO pulls them into one place: bid versions over an editable planning timeline, worksheet scenarios you can duplicate and compare, and dashboards that roll everything up studio by studio.

stories.title: The hardest part
stories.body: The worksheet. Spreadsheet grade UX for 180 shots with per discipline day rates, multi currency totals and four languages, all without a single number drifting. That was the deep end of this build.

stackNotes.reason: Four screens of dense UI that all share one state: worksheets, networks, dashboards and settings. React keeps that composable, and the ecosystem covers graphs and charts so nothing gets hand rolled twice.

Bid planning is a live graph at heart. Weekly bids are nodes, dependencies are edges, and the active path lights up through all of it. React Flow handles zoom, selection and edges, so it stays accurate at any shot count.

Production finance thinks in spreadsheets. Rows, filters and totals are how planners read money, so the worksheet speaks that language directly: 180 shots live, formulas in place, and a scenario copy for every what if, with zero retraining.
The studio runs across regions, so the numbers have to survive translation. Labels, dates and currency formatting localize across four languages, and the totals never drift.
